title: Fragmenta ex commentariis in epistulam ad Ephesios Unit 7 opening
english: Some have read "which is the first commandment with a promise" (Ephesians 6:2) as if the commandments before it held no promise. For they think the first promise is set down on this one: "that it may go well with you, and that you may live long on the land which the Lord your God is giving you."

But these readers seem not to have noticed that a promise lies on the second commandment as well. "You shall not make for yourself an idol," it says, "nor a likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or on the earth beneath, or in the waters under the earth. You shall not bow down to them, nor serve them. For I am the Lord your God, a jealous God, repaying the sins of the fathers on the children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me, and showing mercy to thousands, to those who love me and keep my commandments" (Exodus 20:4-6). Observe that "showing mercy to thousands, to those who love me and keep my commandments" is a promise.

Perhaps, then, since the Ten Commandments were given to the people as their first legislation after they came out of Egypt, each of the ten commandments is a first commandment, spoken among the first of all that followed.

Yet someone who wants to hold to the plain sense of "which is the first commandment with a promise" will say this: the promise "that you may live long on the land which the Lord your God is giving you" belongs properly to the commandment "Honor your father and your mother"; but "showing mercy to thousands, to those who love me and keep my commandments" does not belong properly to "You shall not make for yourself an idol, nor any likeness."

Then again, the one who explains the whole Decalogue as made up of first commandments will object to this too. He will say that long life on the land which the Lord God gives to the saints is not given for the one commandment "Honor your father and your mother" alone, but for countless others as well. And such a person will need to gather the commandments to which "that you may live long on the land which the Lord your God is giving you" is attached.

After this we must inquire about the promise that grants long life on the land which the Lord God gives to the saints. We should not fail to see that the Jews think this comes about according to the letter. But we see that this is by no means true; the prophet too says, "Woe is me, that my sojourning has been prolonged" (Psalm 120:5). So we must look for the good land which the Lord God gives by promise to the one who has left the spiritual Egypt, who has traveled with all patience and endurance through the spiritual wilderness, great and terrible, and who has conquered the great kings whom the Lord strikes down and the mighty kings whom the Lord has slain.

"And you masters, do the same things to them" (Ephesians 6:9). Origen says: Which of the things said before are "the same things"? I think, then, that they are "in simplicity of heart," "doing the will of God," "from the soul," and "with goodwill" toward the household servants.

"Finally, be strong in the Lord and in the might of his strength" (Ephesians 6:10). To be made strong in the Lord is to be made strong in the Word, in wisdom, in the contemplation of the truth, and in all the aspects of Christ. Of these the greatest is the might of his strength, mightier than virtue and its kinds, all of which are powers, just as the vices are powerlessness. Among the virtues, as those skilled in these matters say, there is one that is not a matter of theory, called strength, so named because it bears some likeness to bodily strength; and another that is a matter of theory, called beauty, named from bodily beauty. It is with this beauty in view that we read, "Gird your sword upon your thigh, O mighty one, in your comeliness and your beauty" (Psalm 45:3); and in the Song of Songs, to the bride, "You are all beautiful, my companion, and there is no blemish in you" (Song of Solomon 4:7); and again in Psalm 45, "And the king will desire your beauty" (Psalm 45:11).
